LEADERSHIP gathered that the fire outbreak occurred in the early hours of Wednesday at Ile Hausa, Opomolu Area, Ilorin .
The fire affected eight shops and two container shops as the personnel of the Kwara State Fire Service worked tirelessly to bring the situation under control and minimise damage.
The spokesman of the State Fire Service, Hakeem Adekunle who confirmed the incision said they received a distress call and turned out at 00:35hrs, following the report of the fire outbreak in Opo- Malu, Ilorin.
He said the incident occurred at a shopping complex comprising approximately 10 shops and two container shops.
“Upon arrival, our firefighters immediately commenced firefighting operations to contain the inferno and prevent it from spreading to adjoining properties.
“The fire affected eight shops and two container shops, while our personnel worked tirelessly to bring the situation under control and minimise further damage.
“Preliminary information gathered at the scene suggests that the fire may have been triggered by a power surge. However, investigations are still ongoing, as other possible factors are also being examined to establish the actual cause of the incident,” Adekunle said.
The Chief Fire Officer,Alabi Muhammed, urged traders, shop owners and operators of small businesses to take fire safety precautions seriously, particularly those involved in cooking and other activities that require open flames.
He advised operators of local restaurants and food businesses that use charcoal, firewood or other traditional cooking methods to ensure that all cooking materials and sources of heat are completely extinguished after use before leaving their premises.
